title: The role of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi in shaping ecosystem services in agroecosystems
content:
This figure summarizes the main findings of the meta-analysis regarding the effects of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) on ecosystem services in agroecosystems as compared to the control (absence of AMF) in different abiotic scenarios.


Abstract

Intensive agriculture contributes to biodiversity loss, soil degradation and the decline of ecosystem services, creating a need for management strategies that sustain crop production while reducing environmental impacts. Arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi are often proposed as biological tools for sustainable agriculture, but their contribution to ecosystem service provision in agroecosystems remains context dependent and unevenly quantified. Here, we compiled 1390 effect-size observations from 115 articles published between 1992 and January 2024. Notably, 91.2% of these observations derived from greenhouse studies, with only 123 representing field experiments. We used a multilevel meta-analysis to assess AM fungal effects on provisioning, regulation and maintenance services classified according to the Common International Classification of Ecosystem Services framework. We also evaluated whether these effects varied with water availability and fertilization level. AM fungi significantly enhanced the accumulation of beneficial substances, buffering against abiotic stress and belowground biomass-related variables, whereas effects on production, nutrient accumulation and soil retention were not significant in the general model. Water-retention proxies showed a negative overall response, although this effect was not significant under drought stress. AM fungal benefits were stronger under drought stress, particularly for plant stress-buffering responses, while high fertilization reduced detectable benefits. These results show that AM fungi can support several ecosystem-service-related processes in agroecosystems, but that their effects are not uniformly positive across all services and depend strongly on abiotic context. We conclude that AM fungi should be considered as components of integrated agroecosystem management strategies, especially under resource-limited conditions, rather than as universal substitutes for external inputs.
